Rep. Scarsdale noted the governor's FY27 budget had just been released and the House was reviewing it, including the per-person line item for senior centers.

decisions.decision: The council agreed to send a letter of support for Rep. Kushmerick's and Rep. Scarsdale's caregiver reform legislation, currently before the Committee on Revenue.
The chair asked members to return with thoughts on criteria for creating honorary/emeritus board member status, suggesting roughly four terms of service as a starting point.
The board agreed to have someone look into trying the 'Plaud Note' AI recording/transcription tool to assist with minutes, without it replacing the work of watching and revising the meeting record.
A flyer time error for the WEAR 365 breakfast presentation (listed as 10am, actually 9am) will be corrected, and Lucas will make a new flyer to be emailed out.
The bylaws subcommittee will hold its first meeting Thursday, using examples from other towns, with discussion to follow at a future council meeting.

The council agreed its role regarding the schools' reading proficiency issue should be limited to organizing volunteer seniors to read with children at the discretion of school educators, not presenting itself as fixing the reading problem.

minutes.headline: State Reps Kushmerick and Scarsdale briefed the COA on caregiver legislation, grants, and school/healthcare funding fights.
minutes.summary: State Representatives Mike Kushmerick and Margaret Scarsdale visited the Council on Aging to discuss caregiver reform legislation, funding sources for home modifications and senior programs, the Nashoba Valley Medical Center closure, and Lunenburg's school funding and reading-proficiency struggles. The board also covered routine business including personnel hiring updates, a telehealth hub project, calendar of upcoming programs, and a lengthy, unresolved-then-resolved debate over how the council should support a proposed seniors-reading-to-students program at the schools, ultimately agreeing to limit its role to organizing volunteer readers.

what_happened.line: The council agreed to send a letter of support for the caregiver reform legislation the two state representatives are sponsoring.
Representatives Kushmerick and Scarsdale said delegation earmarks helped cover part of last year's school budget gap through direct funding.
The council limited its role in a proposed seniors-reading-to-students program to organizing volunteer readers, not addressing school reading proficiency.
A board member pressed the delegation to shift more state aid into the flexible unrestricted general government category instead of separate restricted grants.

why_it_matters: The caregiver bill and grant-versus-flexible-aid debate touch how state money reaches senior services and the town's general budget, not just this board.
